findings.title: Possible NPE when falling back to the all-clients resource
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, if no client-specific resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is called. It returns null when the schema is unsupported (admin permissions disabled, or the server is not the admin-permissions client) or when the 'Clients' resource is missing. The result is passed straight into `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` and then `resource.getScopes()` with no null check. That produces an NPE, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a plain 'no permission' (false). Add a null check on `resource` before using it.

findings.title: Fallback to all-clients permission happens only when no client-specific resource exists
findings.body: The all-clients ('Clients' type) resource is consulted only when no resource exists for the individual client. Once any permission references that client, a resource is created for it and evaluation runs only against that resource. A broad grant on all clients (for example MANAGE or VIEW) is then ignored for that client unless the per-client evaluation happens to merge it in. The tests only cover per-client and all-clients cases separately, so this mixed scenario is untested. It also differs from how the Users tests expect fallback to 'all-users' to work.

findings.title: Listener now gated on V1 feature flag; behavior change and V2 still throws
findings.body: The cleanup listener is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously it ran unconditionally. Role, client and group removal no longer disable and clean up permissions when only V1 is off. If both V1 and V2 features are on, `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` and `clients().setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so deleting a client fails. Selecting the behavior by feature flag this way is fragile. The V2 variant should be a no-op, or the check should be on the evaluator type rather than the flag.

findings.title: Several ClientPermissionEvaluator methods throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2
findings.body: `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, `canExchangeTo` and others throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Existing callers, such as the client 'management/permissions' endpoint and token-exchange checks, call these unconditionally. With V2 enabled they will return 500s instead of a clean 'not supported' 4xx or a false result. Callers should be guarded, or these methods should return safe defaults such as `false` or an empty map.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never used. The `logger` field and the imports `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity` and `DefaultEvaluationContext` exist only for that dead code or are unused. Remove them.

findings.title: Javadoc on require* methods says 'Returns true'
findings.body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are `void` methods that throw ForbiddenException. Their Javadoc says 'Returns `true` if ...'. It should say they throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding `can*` method returns false.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` special-cases only the Users type (translating ids to usernames and 'All users'). For Clients permissions it falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Client resources are named by internal id, so this likely returns null or an opaque id when permissions are listed. The 'Clients' all-resource has no friendly label either, so Clients permissions will show up inconsistently with Users ones.

findings.title: Mixes JUnit4 fail with JUnit5 tests
findings.body: The test imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` (JUnit 4) in a JUnit 5 class, while the rest of the suite uses `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`. Tests also do not cover deny scenarios for CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the all-clients plus single-client mix, or the VIEW-all-clients fallback for individual client permissions.
